subject: E2E latency validation scenarios and test schedule
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@cobalthealth.com>, SaaS Ops <ops@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: E2E latency validation scenarios and test schedule

Thanks for the productive call earlier — quick recap and concrete next steps so we can align expectations before we run the validation tests.

Recap (what we heard)
- Target SLOs: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 750ms for typical 512-token requests (including network hop to your app and our hosted API).
- Peak concurrency envelope: 120 concurrent active sessions during daytime peak, sustained bursts to 250 for short windows (<= 3 minutes).
- Streaming usage: ~35% of requests use streaming (partial results), mostly single-stream, with average response lengths ~300 tokens.
- Current provider reported numbers: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.1s (Elaine please confirm if these are 95/99 values for E2E).

Proposed validation plan (agreed on call)
1) Baseline run (your current provider) — Cobalt to provide a 10k-sample baseline CSV of request sizes and timestamps (we referenced p95-p99-baseline-results.csv).
2) Traffic synthesis — Redwood will run three scenarios: steady-state 120 concurrency, ramp-to-burst 250 concurrency (3 min bursts), and streaming-heavy (50% streaming) using the attached traffic-scenarios.yml.
3) Metrics to capture: client-side end-to-end latency (including retransmits), server processing token time, tail-queue delays, and error rate.
4) Acceptance: p95 <= 350ms and p99 <= 750ms for the steady-state scenario; for burst scenario we agreed to allow p99 up to 1.2s if overall error rate < 0.1%.

Action items and owners
- Cobalt (Elaine / Ops): confirm baseline CSV and current provider p95/p99 exports — due Thu, Apr 22 EOD.
- Redwood (Marissa): schedule validation window and provide test harness + do-not-disturb IP list — due Fri, Apr 23.
- Redwood Eng (Ben + Jonas): prepare canary test plan and failure/fallback criteria for streaming — due Mon, Apr 26.

Attachments: p95-p99-baseline-results.csv (placeholder), traffic-scenarios.yml
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-cobalt-latency-tests

If anything above doesn't match what you heard, flag it and we'll update. Otherwise we'll plan to kick off the baseline ingest on Apr 23 and run the Redwood-hosted validation on Apr 26.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items and a couple clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline numbers: the p95/p99 I quoted on the call were aggregated from our frontend telemetry (browser -> app -> provider). Our CSV export has per-request timings; we'll share a trimmed 10k-sample file (anonymized) by Thu 22 Apr as requested.
- Concurrency: 120 steady-state is correct. The 250 bursts are what our marketing events drive; those are short (90–180s) and mostly read-only requests which stress the tail.
- Streaming: streaming sessions are used for long-form summaries; they average 300 tokens but can spike to 1k tokens for certain requests. For the streaming-heavy scenario please include one test with 1k token sequences to surface KV-cache pressure.
- Non-functional: we also want to ensure that retry behavior and HTTP connection pooling are considered when you measure client-side E2E.

Attachments we will send Thursday: p95-p99-baseline-results.csv (sample), plus a short note explaining how we instrument latency (headers to look for).

On our side, if Redwood can provide an estimated run duration and an IP allowlist by Friday, we will schedule ops to open the test window on Apr 26 morning.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Reliability, Cobalt Health

Looping in engineering notes from the pre-test design perspective — copying the relevant bit of Elaine's message inline for reference.

> On Tue, 20 Apr 2027 at 18:14 Elaine Park <elaine.park@cobalthealth.com> wrote:
> > For the streaming-heavy scenario please include one test with 1k token sequences to surface KV-cache pressure.

High level test requirements (engineering)
- We need the baseline CSV in the same schema we'll use for the traffic replayer (columns: client_ts, request_id, token_count, route, streaming_flag). Please confirm column names — if Cobalt's export differs, we'll map it but prefer the schema above.
- Canary plan: run low-traffic canary on Redwood-hosted for 1 hour (steady-state 20 concurrency) to validate correctness, then scale to full steady-state and run burst tests. Canary must include streaming paths.
- Observability hooks: we will instrument a synthetic header X-Redwood-Test-Id so Cobalt can correlate logs. Also request that Cobalt adds the tracer-id header to their ingress so we can stitch traces.
- Failure/fallback: if p99 exceeds 1.5s for >5% of requests during burst scenario, abort and collect full trace dump; fallback to incumbent routing for the remainder of the window.

Engineering to-do (Jonas)
- Generate traffic replay job + verify tokenization matches model variant used in hosted run.
- Prepare a microbenchmark to quantify KV cache warm-up for 1k-token streaming runs.

Marissa — I'll draft the canary test plan and attach it to the drive folder by EOD; we should send IP ranges and expected test duration to Elaine once that's ready.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Elaine and Ben — plan looks good. Final coordination notes and timeline: 

Schedule
- Thu Apr 22: Cobalt provides baseline CSV + instrumentation notes (Elaine).
- Fri Apr 23: Redwood posts canary plan + IP allowlist and estimated run durations (Ben/Jonas).
- Mon Apr 26 09:00–13:00 PT: Canary window (20 concurrency), followed by steady-state 120 concurrency run.
- Mon Apr 26 14:30–15:00 PT: Burst scenario and streaming-heavy runs.

Acceptance mapping (explicit)
- Steady-state: pass if p95 <= 350ms AND p99 <= 750ms AND error rate < 0.1% (measured client-side).
- Burst: pass if p95 <= 500ms AND p99 <= 1.2s OR p99 <= 1.5s with documented fallback performed and RTO < 30m.
- Streaming-heavy: measure token-throughput and KV-warmup; we will capture per-token processing time and report median token time.

Drive: added canary-test-plan.pdf (high level runbook) and a stub CSV p95-p99-baseline-results.csv for schema reference. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-cobalt-latency-tests

If all good, we'll treat Thursday's baseline drop as the gating artifact and proceed with canary Friday. Please reply-all with any blocking concerns.
